title: Neural Belief-Matching Decoding for Topological Quantum Error Correction Codes
summary: Quantum error correction (QEC) is critical for scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing. Topological codes, such as the toric code, offer hardware-efficient architectures but their Tanner graphs contain many girth-4 cycles that degrade the performance of belief-propagation (BP) decoding. For this reason, BP decoding is typically followed by a more complex second stage decoder such as minimum-weight perfect matching.
